1	# Session Handoff — 2026-08-12 SDD/Spec-Drift Initiative
2	
3	This session ran a comprehensive spec-driven-development (SDD) initiative across the whole
4	workspace: build a semantic-model reference layer, draft formal `spec@1` documents via the real
5	`canon` plugin pipeline, validate current code against those specs, and fix what the validation
6	found. It ran long and built a lot of context — this doc is the handoff so a fresh session can
7	pick up without re-deriving any of it.
8	
9	## Starter prompt for the next session
10	
11	> Read `docs/superpowers/session-handoff-2026-08-12.md` for full context, then: (1) review the
12	> uncommitted changes with `git status`/`git diff` and commit them if they look right to you —
13	> commit message should summarize the bug fixes and test-coverage closure, not just say "SDD
14	> work"; (2) the CLI spec test-coverage gaps (see "What's still open" below) are the best next
15	> target if you want to keep closing gaps — SPEC-CLI-001a alone has ~15 uncovered criteria;
16	> (3) alternatively, run `canon-drift-checker` again against the newly-added tests from this
17	> session (nothing has adversarially re-verified them yet) if the priority is confidence over
18	> coverage. Ask me which before starting substantial work.
19	
20	## What was done, in order
21	
22	1. **Phase 1 — Semantic model.** `.claude/semantic-model/` (7 files + `INDEX.md`): one file per
23	   subsystem (pipeline, extractor, resolver, types, serialization, cli, binding), each grounded
24	   in real source with numbered invariants and known gaps. Load via `INDEX.md`'s routing table —
25	   never load all seven at once.
26	
27	2. **Phase 2 — Spec drafting.** All 7 capabilities now have gated `spec@1` documents in
28	   `.claude/specs/`, drafted through the *real* `canon` pipeline (`canon-drafter` →
29	   `canon-verifier` → `canon-auditor` → `canon-exit-gate`), not approximated:
30	   - `SPEC-PIPELINE-001.json`, `SPEC-EXTRACTOR-001.json`, `SPEC-RESOLVER-001.json`,
31	     `SPEC-TYPES-001.json`, `SPEC-SERIALIZATION-001.json`, `SPEC-BINDING-001.json`
32	   - `SPEC-CLI-001a/b/c/d.json` (split from one oversized draft: exit-codes / atomic writes /
33	     LSP framing / config loading) — **already committed** as `df68cf1`, unlike the rest of
34	     this session's changes.
35	
36	   Several specs took many gate rounds (pipeline hit 9) because the adversarial gate kept
37	   catching real precision errors — worth knowing if you see `revision_note`/`reasoning` fields
38	   in the JSON that read like a long story. That's the gate working as intended, not noise.
39	
40	3. **Phase 3 — Drift validation + fixes.** Ran `canon-drift-checker` against all 7 specs (via
41	   6 parallel agents; CLI's 4 sub-specs bundled into one). Findings were split into
42	   covered / uncovered / **drifted**. Every drifted (= code contradicts spec) finding was
43	   investigated and either fixed in code or fixed in the spec, never left ambiguous.
44	
45	4. **Gap-closing pass** (this was the last major chunk of work, after the user asked to
46	   "make all sets of improvements we can make to close the gaps extensively"). Went
47	   subsystem-by-subsystem adding the missing tests the drift pass identified, verifying each
48	   new test against a deliberately-broken version of the relevant code before trusting it.
49	
50	## Real bugs found and fixed this session (7 total)
51	
52	All have regression tests confirmed to fail against the pre-fix code and pass against the fix.
53	
54	1. **Watch mode was permanently one edit behind.** `WatchSession::update_file` bound
55	   `new_global` directly to `ArcSwap::rcu(...)`'s return value — but `rcu` returns the
56	   *pre-swap* value (`compare_and_swap` convention), not the closure's result. Every
57	   incremental update resolved against stale content. Fixed via `load_full()` after the swap.
58	   `crates/core/src/pipeline/watch.rs`.
59	2. **`watch --out`'s stats were always zero.** `WatchSession::snapshot()` used
60	   `ExtractionStats::default()`. Fixed for `components_extracted`; other stats fields
61	   (files_parsed, duration_ms, etc.) remain a narrower, documented gap — the session doesn't
62	   accumulate them incrementally. Same file.
63	3. **Relative `--config` paths broke when their parent wasn't the invocation cwd.**
64	   `try_load_config` changes the node subprocess's cwd to the config's parent but was passing
65	   the original relative path through unchanged. Fixed via canonicalization before handoff.
66	   `crates/cli/src/config.rs`.
67	4. **Panic containment gap in NAPI auto-vivification.** `initialize_session` /
68	   `extract_file_incremental` / `create_session` ran `WatchSession::new` construction (and, for
69	   `create_session`, the options conversion) *outside* `panic_guard::contain_panic`. Fixed by
70	   moving construction inside the guarded closure in all three. `crates/binding/src/lib.rs`.
71	5. **`extract --out` was never actually atomic** — only `watch --out` got the `write_atomic`
72	   treatment originally; `extract.rs` still called bare `std::fs::write`. Fixed by extracting
73	   `write_atomic` into `crates/cli/src/output.rs` and sharing it.
74	6. **`watch`'s keyboard-quit (`q`/`c`) ignored the tracked exit code**, hardcoding
75	   `process::exit(0)` regardless of whether the run had errors. Fixed to read the tracked
76	   atomic. `crates/cli/src/commands/watch.rs`.
77	7. **LSP verbose-mode stdout corruption.** `tracing::error!` calls wrote ANSI-colored text to
78	   stdout under `-v`/`-vv` — the same channel LSP reserves exclusively for
79	   `Content-Length`-framed protocol messages. Fixed by routing all tracing output to stderr
80	   globally. `crates/cli/src/main.rs`. New integration test file:
81	   `crates/cli/tests/lsp_process.rs`.
82	
83	Two smaller **code-vs-spec alignment fixes** (not bugs, just inconsistency):
84	- `chain.rs`'s non-cyclic depth-exhaustion path now routes through `ResolvedChain::give_up`
85	  (was hand-rolling an equivalent-but-inconsistent path).
86	- `SPEC-EXTRACTOR-001.json`'s AC-023 was corrected — chained conditional types emit one
87	  `MaxDepthExceeded` diagnostic *per child branch* (up to 4), not one per chain; single-child
88	  nesting forms (the common case) still emit exactly one. Both behaviors now have tests.
89	
90	## New process guidance added
91	
92	`CLAUDE.md` gained a "Testing discipline" section with two rules, both directly motivated by
93	what caused today's bugs to survive prior review passes:
94	1. **Sibling-path parity** — a function mirroring an already-tested one (e.g. `update_file()`
95	   mirrors `extract()`) needs its own equivalent test, not just "doesn't crash."
96	2. **Assert content, not presence** — prefer `assert_eq!` against exact values over
97	   `contains()`/`is_some()` liveness checks wherever the cost is comparable.
98	
99	## Test/quality state as of end of session
100	
101	- **357 tests passing** across the whole workspace (up from a much smaller baseline — see
102	  `docs/STATUS.md` for the pre-session count, which is now stale and due for an update).
103	- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean.
104	- `cargo fmt --all -- --check` clean.
105	- New dev-dependency: `trybuild` (added to `crates/core/Cargo.toml`) for a compile-fail test
106	  proving `ParsedProp`'s sealed-constructor invariant.
107	- New test files: `crates/cli/tests/lsp_process.rs`,
108	  `crates/core/tests/compile_fail.rs` + `crates/core/tests/compile_fail/parsed_prop_seal.rs`.
109	
110	## What's still open (tracked, not blocking)
111	
112	All entries below are already recorded in `docs/edge-cases.md` — check there for exact
113	citations before re-discovering them:
114	
115	- **`resolve_named` has no cycle detection** (unlike `resolve_props_chain`) — bounded only by
116	  `MAX_DEPTH=20`, no dedicated diagnostic. `resolver/named.rs`.
117	- **`WatchSession::component_cache` staleness** — two related manifestations (disambiguated-key
118	  entries lingering after edits, renamed components leaving stale old-name entries) trace to
119	  the same root cause: `component_cache.insert(...)` never evicts a file's previous keys.
120	- **DTS cache same-tick/same-size staleness** (P0-2, deliberately deferred, documented in a
121	  code comment on `key_for`).
122	- **Config path with a literal backslash in a directory name** fails via Node's
123	  `pathToFileURL` percent-encoding — narrow edge case, not fixed.
124	- **CLI test coverage is uneven.** SPEC-CLI-001a (exit-code contract) alone still has roughly
125	  15 of its ~21 criteria uncovered by tests, even after this session's gap-closing pass —
126	  triaged down in favor of the LSP fix and the weak-assertion strengthening, which were judged
127	  higher value for the time available. SPEC-CLI-001b/c/d are in better shape but not
128	  exhaustively covered either.
129	- **Today's own new tests haven't been adversarially re-verified.** Every one was confirmed to
130	  fail-then-pass against its specific fix, which is solid TDD discipline, but no independent
131	  `canon-drift-checker`/`canon-exit-gate` pass has tried to find holes in this session's own
132	  additions the way it did for the original 7 specs.
133	
134	## Things to leave alone
135	
136	- `.entire/`, `.gemini/`, `.moon/hooks/*` showing as untracked in `git status` are **not**
137	  from this session — don't assume ownership or clean them up without checking with the user
138	  first.
139	- `.claude/specs/SPEC-CLI-001a/b/c/d.json` are already committed (`df68cf1`) — everything else
140	  in this handoff is still uncommitted, staged nowhere, sitting in the working tree.
141	
142	## Where things live
143	
144	- Specs: `.claude/specs/*.json`
145	- Semantic model: `.claude/semantic-model/*.md` (start at `INDEX.md`)
146	- Bug/gap tracker: `docs/edge-cases.md` (kept current throughout this session — the audit
147	  trail convention is strikethrough + **FIXED**, not deletion)
148	- This doc: `docs/superpowers/session-handoff-2026-08-12.md`

1	//! Structural substitution for user-defined generic type aliases.
2	//!
3	//! `type Assign<T, U> = Omit<T, keyof U> & U` declares type parameters `T`/`U`
4	//! that are opaque names until a call site supplies concrete arguments, e.g.
5	//! `Assign<HTMLProps<'div'>, SelectRootBaseProps<T>>`. Previously the resolver
6	//! looked up `Assign` by name and resolved its body directly — `T`/`U` were
7	//! never replaced with the caller's arguments, so `Omit<T, keyof U>` resolved
8	//! against literal type names `"T"`/`"U"` (unresolvable) instead of the real
9	//! types, and the whole component's props came back empty.
10	//!
11	//! This module walks the alias body's `CollectedType`/`CollectedTypeAlias` tree
12	//! and replaces every bare `Named` reference to a declared parameter with the
13	//! caller's argument, before normal resolution proceeds. Purely structural —
14	//! no type inference, no conditional-type evaluation.
15	
16	use camino::Utf8Path;
17	use rustc_hash::FxHashMap;
18	
19	use crate::types::{
20	    CollectedObjectField, CollectedType, CollectedTypeAlias, Diagnostic, DiagnosticCode, DiagnosticSeverity,
21	};
22	
23	use super::import::resolve_to_canonical;
24	use super::ResolutionContext;
25	
26	/// Map from a generic alias's declared parameter name to the caller-supplied
27	/// argument, each pre-wrapped in `CollectedType::AtFile` pinned to the file the
28	/// argument was actually written in (see that variant's doc comment) — the
29	/// callee alias being substituted into may live in a different file entirely.
30	pub(super) type Substitution<'a> = FxHashMap<&'a str, CollectedType>;
31	
32	/// Build a `Substitution` from declared parameter names and the caller's
33	/// arguments, tagging each argument with `origin_file` — the file the *caller*
34	/// wrote them in, which is where any further name lookups on them must happen.
35	///
36	/// If `params` declares more type parameters than `args` supplies (a call site
37	/// under-applying a generic alias, e.g. `Foo<string>` for `type Foo<T, U> = ...`),
38	/// the trailing unfilled parameters are silently dropped from the substitution —
39	/// pushes a `Warning` diagnostic naming them so this doesn't degrade silently.
40	pub(super) fn build_substitution<'a>(
41	    params: &'a [compact_str::CompactString],
42	    args: &[CollectedType],
43	    origin_file: &Utf8Path,
44	    diagnostics: &mut Vec<Diagnostic>,
45	) -> Substitution<'a> {
46	    if params.len() > args.len() {
47	        let unfilled: Vec<&str> = params[args.len()..].iter().map(|p| p.as_str()).collect();
48	        diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
49	            severity: DiagnosticSeverity::Warning,
50	            message: format!(
51	                "Generic alias in '{}' declares {} type parameter(s) but only {} were supplied — '{}' left unsubstituted",
52	                origin_file,
53	                params.len(),
54	                args.len(),
55	                unfilled.join("', '")
56	            ),
57	            file: Some(origin_file.to_string()),
58	            line: None,
59	            column: None,
60	            help: Some("Check the call site supplies a type argument for every declared type parameter.".into()),
61	            code: DiagnosticCode::GenericArgumentMismatch,
62	        });
63	    }
64	    params
65	        .iter()
66	        .map(|p| p.as_str())
67	        .zip(args.iter().map(|a| CollectedType::AtFile { file: origin_file.to_owned(), inner: Box::new(a.clone()) }))
68	        .collect()
69	}

# Drift report — SPEC-RESOLVER-001

Spec: /Users/gabe/Projects/oxc-react-codegen/.claude/specs/SPEC-RESOLVER-001.json
Workspace: /Users/gabe/Projects/oxc-react-codegen
Verdict: No implementation drift. Every criterion's implementation matches what the spec says. Test coverage is the problem: 6 of 8 criteria have tests asserting materially less than the criterion demands.

Working tree is clean. I temporarily added two probe tests to crates/core/src/resolver/mod.rs to empirically verify two claims, then reverted via `git checkout`; 62 resolver tests pass.

## covered (2)

AC-1 — source-defined interface beats known-pattern shortcut via `extends`
- Impl: /Users/gabe/Projects/oxc-react-codegen/crates/core/src/resolver/chain.rs:106-136 routes through the shared /Users/gabe/Projects/oxc-react-codegen/crates/core/src/resolver/precedence.rs:39-65, which checks type alias -> interface -> known in that fixed order.
- Tests: resolver/mod.rs:548 asserts `entry.props.contains_key("customSx")`; precedence.rs:79 asserts the returned variant is `SourceOrKnownMatch::Interface`.
- Assertion strength adequate. The criterion's contract IS "customSx is a resolved prop", and the negative clause ("does NOT substitute the known shortcut") is entailed — the MUI SxProps shortcut yields an opaque type contributing zero props, so customSx cannot exist unless the project's interface won.

AC-1b — same precedence at the resolve_named call site
- Impl: /Users/gabe/Projects/oxc-react-codegen/crates/core/src/resolver/named.rs:55-59 returns PropType::Named on an interface match, via the identical shared precedence call at named.rs:42-43.
- Test: resolver/mod.rs:614 asserts `matches!(&sx_prop.prop_type, PropType::Named { name, .. } if name == "SxProps")` — the criterion's exact stated shape.

## uncovered (6) — implementation correct, tests too weak

AC-2b — non-cyclic MAX_DEPTH exhaustion (the criterion you asked about)

THE ALIGNMENT HOLDS. chain.rs:28-31 now reads:
    let diag = super::max_depth_diagnostic(&format!("type '{}'", type_name), consuming_file);
    return ResolvedChain::give_up(type_name.to_owned(), Some(diag), state);
`give_up` (resolver/mod.rs:386-391) pushes the diagnostic and returns `empty_with_compose(type_name)`. `max_depth_diagnostic` (resolver/mod.rs:55-65) is Warning / MaxDepthExceeded / "Max resolution depth exceeded resolving {what}". I verified the end-to-end product empirically with a temporary probe on a 26-deep distinct-interface chain:
    composes=["Level21"]  diags=[(Warning, MaxDepthExceeded, "Max resolution depth exceeded resolving type 'Level21'")]
That matches the criterion exactly. The "never ResolvedChain::default()" clause is additionally enforced structurally — ResolvedChain has no Default impl (resolver/mod.rs:346-357, deliberate per the doc comment at 360-365), so that branch cannot compile.

BUT NO TEST ASSERTS THE OUTPUT/SHAPE. resolver/mod.rs:2575 (test_non_cyclic_depth_exhaustion_emits_max_depth_diagnostic) discards the entry with `let (_entry, diagnostics) = ...` and asserts only the diagnostic triple. The diagnostic half is asserted exactly (severity + code + message substring — good). The give_up half — `composes` populated with the type name, which is give_up's only observable effect beyond the push, and which reaches ComponentEntry.composes (types/output.rs:103, populated at resolver/mod.rs:335) — is unasserted. DOWNGRADED SPECIFICALLY FOR THIS GAP. Fix: add `assert_eq!(entry.composes, vec!["Level21".to_string()]);`

Two things worth knowing about this hunk specifically:
1. The change was BEHAVIOR-PRESERVING. Pre-fix (`git show 7357431 -- crates/core/src/resolver/chain.rs`) was `state.diagnostics.push(max_depth_diagnostic(...)); return ResolvedChain::empty_with_compose(type_name.to_owned());` — byte-for-byte what give_up does internally. No test can distinguish pre-fix from post-fix code. The commit message's claim "Every fix has a regression test confirmed to fail against the pre-fix code and pass against the fix" cannot hold for this hunk; it was a consistency refactor, not a fix. Nothing is wrong with the code — but do not count test_non_cyclic_depth_exhaustion_emits_max_depth_diagnostic as a regression test for it.
2. AC-2b's clause "produced via ResolvedChain::give_up" is NOT EXTERNALLY FALSIFIABLE as written — it names an internal construction path, not observable behavior. Only its effects (composes + diagnostic) are checkable. A canon-gate escape worth noting: the criterion should be restated in terms of the observable composes/diagnostic pair.

AC-2 — cycle detection (worst gap of the set)
- Impl correct and complete: chain.rs:38-55 emits Info / MaxDepthExceeded / "Circular type reference detected resolving '{}' in '{}' — stopping here to avoid infinite recursion" via give_up.
- Test resolver/mod.rs:2517 asserts only `diagnostics.iter().any(|d| d.message.to_lowercase().contains("circular"))` plus `entry.props.contains_key("id")`.
- DOWNGRADED FOR WEAK ASSERTIONS. The criterion demands four things the test never checks: Info severity, DiagnosticCode::MaxDepthExceeded, the exact phrase "Circular type reference detected" (the test's case-insensitive "circular" would also match the HELP text of an unrelated max_depth_diagnostic, or any future rewording), and the give_up shape (composes == ["LoopProps"]). `contains_key("id")` is a presence check that survives the prop resolving to garbage.

AC-3 — multi-parameter function degrade
- Impl correct: resolver/func.rs:64-79 builds `raw = format!("({}) => {}", param_strs.join(", "), return_type.to_raw_string())` and embeds it in an Info diagnostic.
- Tests: resolver/mod.rs:2227 asserts Opaque(MultiParamFunction) exactly (that half is fine). resolver/mod.rs:2247 asserts the diagnostic with `assert!(!state.diagnostics.is_empty(), ...)`.
- DOWNGRADED FOR WEAK ASSERTIONS. AC-3 is the most precisely-worded criterion in the spec — it demands the message contain the byte-for-byte format! output — and the test is a bare non-empty check that would pass on ANY diagnostic from ANY source, including a spurious unresolvable-import warning. For the test's own fixture (String, Number params, Void return; to_raw_string at types/collected.rs:136-147) the exact expected substring is `(string, number) => void`, and neither Info severity nor that substring is asserted.

AC-4 — LiteralUnion as props base
- Impl correct: resolver/alias.rs:114-133 — Warning / DiagnosticCode::OpaqueType, message contains "is a literal union and can't be used as a component's props base in '{}' — expected an interface, intersection, union, or inline object type", i.e. both required substrings in the required order, via give_up.
- Test resolver/mod.rs:2632 asserts only `d.message.contains("literal union")`.
- DOWNGRADED FOR WEAK ASSERTIONS. Severity, code, the full first substring, the second substring, and the ordering are all unasserted — "literal union" matches a two-word fragment of a message the criterion specifies at ~120 characters.

AC-5 — under-applied generic type arguments
- Impl correct: resolver/substitute.rs:46-68 — Warning / GenericArgumentMismatch, names every unfilled param, and the .zip() at line 67 structurally cannot create an entry for an unfilled parameter.
- Test substitute.rs:325 asserts `subst.len() == 1`, `diagnostics.len() == 1`, `severity == Warning`, `message.contains('U')`.
- DOWNGRADED FOR WEAK ASSERTIONS, though this is the mildest of the six. Missing: DiagnosticCode::GenericArgumentMismatch is named by the criterion and never asserted. And "contains no entry for any unfilled parameter" is asserted only as `len() == 1` — a map of {"U": ...} also has length 1; `assert!(!subst.contains_key("U"))` is the assertion the criterion actually demands. `message.contains('U')` is a single-CHAR search that happens to be sound only because no other uppercase U appears in this fixture's message.

AC-6 — template-literal Cartesian-product cap
- Impl correct: resolver/template.rs:106 returns None past MAX_TEMPLATE_LITERAL_EXPANSIONS (4096, template.rs:49); template.rs:29-39 degrades to Info / TemplateLiteralOpaque / "Template literal type '{}' could not be statically expanded" with OpaqueReason::TemplateLiteral.
- Test template.rs:198 asserts Opaque(TemplateLiteral) and `d.code == TemplateLiteralOpaque`.
- DOWNGRADED FOR WEAK ASSERTIONS. Missing: Info severity and the "could not be statically expanded" substring, both named by the criterion. The "no expanded member list anywhere in the output" clause is partially entailed by the Opaque match (an Opaque is not a LiteralUnion), so that clause is acceptable as-is.

## drifted (0)

No criterion's observable behavior diverges from what the spec specifies.

## Non-goal check (as requested)

NO DRIFT. The spec handles the accepted resolve_named gap correctly. non_goals[0] states it explicitly, scope[2] narrows named.rs to "the shared precedence function only (not its cycle-detection behavior, which is a documented non-goal)", and I read all 8 criteria — none asserts or implies that resolve_named detects cycles or emits a dedicated diagnostic. AC-1b touches resolve_named for precedence only. The citation is accurate: docs/edge-cases.md:63 still lists it as "Still open", matching named.rs:25 (bounded only by `depth > MAX_DEPTH`).

## Adjacent finding — empirically confirmed, not covered by any criterion

`state.visited` (chain.rs:38) is insert-only; never unwound when a subtree finishes. So a VISITED-KEY HIT DOES NOT IMPLY A CYCLE — plain diamond inheritance trips it. Confirmed with a temporary probe (CProps extends A, B; A extends Base; B extends Base; no cycle anywhere):

    props=["a","b","c","shared"]
    composes=["Base"]
    diags=[(Info, "Circular type reference detected resolving 'Base' in '/test/diamond.tsx' — stopping here to avoid infinite recursion")]

Props survive intact (Base's props already arrived via A's branch, and merge_parent dedupes by name), so this is not a correctness bug in the output — but it emits a false "circular reference" diagnostic and puts Base in composes for a perfectly ordinary TypeScript pattern. Notably, alias.rs:52 and alias.rs:291 already CLONE the visited set to branch, precisely to avoid this class of false positive in union contexts; the diamond-extends path never got the same treatment. A sibling-path gap of exactly the shape CLAUDE.md's rule 1 describes. It undermines AC-2's premise, though it violates no criterion as written. Suggest tracking it in docs/edge-cases.md next to the named.rs entry rather than treating it as a SPEC-RESOLVER-001 finding.

## Summary

The chain.rs give_up alignment you asked about IS GENUINE AND CORRECT — I verified the depth-exhaustion path produces composes=["Level21"] plus a Warning/MaxDepthExceeded/"Max resolution depth exceeded" diagnostic, exactly matching give_up's contract, and the "never ResolvedChain::default()" clause is enforced by the type system rather than merely tested. Two caveats: no test asserts that path's returned shape (only its diagnostic), and the change was behavior-preserving, so it has no regression test and cannot have one as written.

Your general worry about this session's tests is CONFIRMED and it is the dominant finding. Implementation matches spec on all 8 criteria — zero behavioral drift — but 6 of 8 fail the "asserts the exact contract" bar, and the pattern is consistent: every criterion specifies a diagnostic's severity AND code AND exact message substring, and the tests assert at most one of the three (AC-3 and AC-4 assert essentially none). The fixes are real; the tests confirm the fixes ran rather than confirming what they produced. Highest-value repairs in order: AC-3 (assert message contains "(string, number) => void"), AC-4 (both substrings + Warning + OpaqueType), AC-2 (severity + code + exact phrase + composes), then AC-2b/AC-6/AC-5 severity-and-code additions.

CLI review complete with much deeper coverage now. Here's what the closer pass found — several genuinely significant gaps I hadn't surfaced before.

## CLI: substantial new findings

**SPEC-CLI-001b (atomic writes) — worse than I first reported.** I'd only flagged a narrow gap. Actually: **AC-002, AC-003, and AC-004 have zero test coverage at any level.** `write_atomic` itself is well-tested in isolation (3 tests), but no test ever calls `cmd_extract` with `--out` and inspects the resulting file, triggers a write failure through the CLI layer, or exercises rename-step cleanup through the actual call site. A regression reverting `extract --out` to bare `fs::write` would pass every test in the suite.

**SPEC-CLI-001c (LSP) — 5 of 9 criteria untested.** I traced the actual source (`read_content_length`'s `Ok(None)` vs `Err(())` split) and confirmed the *implementation* genuinely matches all 9 criteria exactly — this is correct, careful code. But:
- **AC-002** (exact-16MiB-boundary frame gets a real response) is only checked at the `check_content_length(16777216).is_ok()` unit level — no test actually sends a full 16MiB body and confirms it's dispatched and answered.
- **AC-005b, AC-005c, AC-005d** (truncated header before the blank line; truncated body; non-UTF-8 header bytes) — I grepped the entire test tree and found nothing for any of these three specific scenarios.
- **AC-006, AC-007** (malformed JSON body / missing `method` field don't desync the stream — a subsequent well-formed frame still gets answered) — also completely untested; no test sends two frames in sequence to prove the loop recovers.

**SPEC-CLI-001d (config) — the one security-relevant criterion is untested.** AC-001 requires that a `--config` path containing quotes, backslashes, or a literal `');process.exit(1);('` payload can't inject JS into the evaluated script. I confirmed the implementation is correct by source (`.env("__DOCGEN_CONFIG_PATH", path)` — genuinely passed via env var, not string concatenation, matching CLAUDE.md's own documented decision). But there's no adversarial test that actually constructs such a path and proves it — the only proof is "the mechanism used structurally can't be vulnerable," not a test exercising the vulnerable-looking case directly.

None of this is drift — every implementation I traced is correct. It's all coverage: real gaps that predate this session in some cases (CLI-001c's malformed-frame handling, CLI-001d's injection safety), not things the session's bug fixes introduced.

I'll hold off re-confirming BINDING/EXTRACTOR/SERIALIZATION further unless you want it — those already got a fairly rigorous pass and I don't have specific reason to doubt them the way CLI's breadth warranted a second look. I found three more real gaps in EXTRACTOR from checking the remaining ~15 criteria I'd originally skipped. BINDING and SERIALIZATION, by contrast, already got the full criterion-by-criterion treatment in my first pass (unlike CLI, which I'd shortcut) — re-checking them didn't turn up anything new.

## EXTRACTOR: 3 more real findings

**AC-009 (malformed `Omit`/`Pick`/`Partial`/`Readonly`) has zero real coverage.** The only test in its vicinity, `record_skip_pushes_an_info_diagnostic_with_the_given_code`, calls `collector.record_skip(...)` *directly* on an empty source string — it never actually parses a malformed generic alias through `parse_file()`. It proves the `record_skip` helper mechanically works, not that AC-009's detection logic ever fires for real malformed input like `type Bad = Omit<OnlyOneArg>`. No test exercises the actual criterion.

**AC-021 and AC-027 both have the same "checked the key, not the value" gap.** 
- AC-021 (`test_two_aliases_to_the_same_base_component_both_survive`) verifies both aliases end up present by name and the base is gone — but never checks that either alias actually carries the base's props type name (`ButtonProps`), which is half of what the criterion requires.
- AC-027 (`test_display_name_update`) verifies the renamed entry exists (`btn.is_some()`) but never checks it still carries the pre-rename props type name (`BtnProps`) — the criterion's central "carrying the same props type name" clause is unverified.

Both are instances of exactly the "assert content, not presence" failure your own CLAUDE.md calls out — interesting that it shows up even in pre-existing tests, not just the newly-added ones.

**Revised EXTRACTOR tally**, now covering all 27 criteria rather than just the 11 new tests: solid coverage on most of the base pattern-detection criteria (AC-001/002/003/005/006/007/010/011/012 all check exact `props_type_name` values via real fixtures), but AC-009 (no coverage), AC-021 and AC-027 (presence-only) join the earlier AC-014/022/024/026 weak spots.

Nothing here is drift — every implementation trace I did confirms the code is correct. It's all test-coverage precision, the same pattern throughout this whole review.

=== AC-001 ===
All substring-based exclusion checks in this criterion (the built-in patterns, exclude_patterns, and the node_modules-string exception) match against the walk-emitted path string reported for each candidate file BEFORE canonicalization — not against the canonicalized file_path that ultimately appears in output.components. These two strings normally agree, but can diverge for a src_dir reached through a symlink (see the negative pair below), so 'full path' throughout this criterion means that pre-canonicalization walk-emitted string specifically. Given a PipelineOptions.src_dirs containing one or more directories that exist on disk, extract() returns an ExtractionOutput whose components include every React component declared in every .ts/.tsx file reachable under those directories, excluding files whose pre-canonicalization walk-emitted path contains any of the plain substrings '.stories.', '.test.', '.spec.', '__snapshots__', or 'node_modules' (unless a src_dir's configured path string itself contains 'node_modules' as a substring, in which case the 'node_modules' substring exclusion is skipped for that src_dir's walk), excluding any file whose pre-canonicalization walk-emitted path contains a user-supplied entry from options.exclude_patterns as a substring, and, when PipelineOptions.exclude_prefixes is non-empty, excluding any component whose display_name starts with any of its entries (see non_goals for this filter's exact semantics — it is a deliberate, silent, user-opted-in exclusion, not a failure case). Additionally, using only fixture-observable input/output pairs: (1) given a src_dir inside a real git work tree (a `.git` directory present in the src_dir or an ancestor of it) containing a `.gitignore` file (in the src_dir itself or any ancestor directory up to the work tree root) that matches a candidate file, that file is excluded from the output — UNLESS that src_dir's configured path string itself contains 'node_modules' as a substring, in which case NO `.gitignore` file at any level (the src_dir's own, any ancestor's, or any nested directory's within the walk) excludes anything from that src_dir's walk, regardless of whether the src_dir or any directory beneath it has its own `.git` directory: every such file IS included in the output. Separately and independently: when that src_dir's path string contains 'node_modules' AND the src_dir itself has no `.git` directory of its own, `.git/info/exclude` also does not exclude anything for that src_dir's walk — UNLESS some directory nested beneath the src_dir (not the src_dir itself) has its own `.git` directory, in which case that nested subtree's own `.git/info/exclude` file DOES still exclude matching files within that nested subtree specifically. As a negative pair: a src_dir that is physically located inside a node_modules directory on disk, but whose configured path string does NOT contain the substring 'node_modules' (e.g. reached via a relative path or symlink whose literal string doesn't include it), is NOT exempt from any of the above — ordinary `.gitignore`/`.git/info/exclude` behavior (ancestor-.git-gated, as in the non-node_modules case) applies to it. Separately, and independent of gitignore handling entirely: because every substring exclusion in this criterion matches against the pre-canonicalization walk-emitted path (per the note at the top of this criterion), a matching file under such a src_dir is included in output.components even though its canonicalized file_path — computed after the exclusion check runs — does contain the substring 'node_modules'; a tester checking output.components purely by scanning file_path strings for 'node_modules' would incorrectly expect this file to have been excluded, but it is not; (2) given a src_dir (in or out of a git work tree, under node_modules or not) containing an `.ignore` file that matches a candidate file, that file is excluded from the output, with no exception; (3) given a src_dir that is NOT inside any git work tree at all (no `.git` directory anywhere in its ancestry) containing a `.gitignore` file that matches a candidate file, that file IS included in the output (gitignore rules have no effect outside a git work tree), while an `.ignore` file in the same non-git-work-tree src_dir still excludes matching files per (2).

=== AC-005 ===
Given a src_dir containing a file whose path bytes are not valid UTF-8, extract() completes, returns components from every other, valid file, and includes in its diagnostics at least one entry that identifies the skipped path (by its available lossy/byte representation) rather than omitting any mention of it.

=== AC-015 ===
Given a WatchSession that has completed initialize(), calling update_file() with the path of a file that was atomically replaced (editor writes to a temp file then renames it over the original path) using content that changes one component's props returns an IncrementalUpdate reflecting that component's new props, and a subsequent snapshot() reflects the same updated state — the session does not miss or misinterpret the change as a deletion.

=== AC-019 ===
Given a WatchSession that has completed initialize(), where file G imports a type that is declared only in file F, and F is subsequently deleted from disk: calling update_file() with F's path returns an IncrementalUpdate whose diagnostics include an IoError entry for F. The component(s) previously resolved from F remain present in WatchSession::component_cache and therefore in the next snapshot() call's output (they are not pruned by update_file — a documented staleness gap, closed only by constructing a new WatchSession). F's removal from the session's internal type graph is externally observable through G, not through F itself: a subsequent update_file() call with G's path produces, for the prop/type that used to resolve against F's declaration, either a diagnostic naming the unresolvable reference or an unresolved/opaque prop type in G's re-resolved component — it does not resolve as if F's declaration still existed.

=== AC-020 ===
Given a freshly-constructed WatchSession on which initialize() has never been called, calling snapshot() does not panic and returns an ExtractionOutput with zero components, zero enums, and zero diagnostics. Calling update_file() on such a session does not panic; it returns an IncrementalUpdate whose updated_components contains only the just-parsed changed file's own component(s), and any prop on that component whose type would normally require resolving a cross-file import or an ambient global (e.g. React's own HTMLAttributes, or a type imported from another project file) appears either as an unresolved/opaque prop type or is accompanied by a diagnostic naming the unresolvable reference, rather than being fully resolved as it would be after a real initialize() call.

=== AC-024 ===
Given a WatchSession that has completed initialize(), calling update_file() with the path of a file that exists on disk but whose byte content is not valid UTF-8 (distinct from AC-005, which concerns the discovered file *path* being non-UTF8, not its contents) returns an IncrementalUpdate with an IoError diagnostic naming that file, and does not panic. updated_components contains no entry whose file_path equals the changed file itself (that file's own component(s), if any existed, are not re-resolved successfully) — but updated_components MAY still contain entries for other files that transitively import the changed file, since those are independently re-resolved as part of the same affected-set walk.

**Resolver — all FIXED:**
- ~~`chain.rs`'s `resolve_interface_chain` shared a single `visited` set across all of an interface's `extends` entries — ordinary diamond inheritance (`interface C extends A, B` where both A and B extend `Base`) was misreported as a cycle, since resolving A's branch marked `Base` visited and B's branch then found it "already visited" and emitted a false "Circular type reference detected" diagnostic, even though `Base` is genuinely shared by two independent parents, not actually cyclic.~~ **FIXED** (found 2026-08-13 via an adversarial `canon-drift-checker` probe, not from any spec criterion): each `extends` entry now resolves against its own cloned `visited` set (mirroring `alias.rs`'s existing `Omit<T, keyof U>`/union-discriminant branch pattern), preserving real cycle detection within a branch while letting sibling branches independently reach a shared ancestor. Test: `diamond_inheritance_does_not_falsely_report_a_cycle` (confirmed to fail against the pre-fix shared-`visited` code before being confirmed against the fix). `chain.rs:216-241`
- ~~The cycle-detected return path is the one give-up site in `chain.rs` that doesn't follow the established `empty_with_compose` pattern used at every other give-up site in the same file... a genuinely self-referential/mutually-recursive interface pair silently loses all props with zero trace.~~ **FIXED**: now returns `ResolvedChain::give_up` with an explicit Info-severity "Circular type reference detected" diagnostic. `chain.rs:38-41`

Everything is clean workspace-wide. Here's the final summary.

## All 22 findings fixed (AC-017 + the 21 from the follow-up review)

**PIPELINE** (5 items): AC-017's test now actually distinguishes canonical from non-canonical paths via a transitive dependent (confirmed fail→pass against the real bug); AC-016b and AC-010 strengthened to check content, not presence; added 4 new tests for AC-015/019/020/024 (atomic replace, deletion, uninitialized session, non-UTF8 content). AC-001 (gitignore matrix) deliberately deferred — flagged explicitly rather than rushed.

**EXTRACTOR** (5 items): AC-014 now checks the diagnostic names "Wrap"; AC-022/026 check Error severity; AC-024 now covers all 5 named shapes; AC-009 got two genuine end-to-end malformed-`Omit<>` tests (the old one only unit-tested `record_skip` in isolation); AC-021/027 now check `props_type_name` values, not just key survival.

**RESOLVER** (5 items, plus one extra bug): AC-2/2b/3/4/5/6 all strengthened to check exact severity/code/message. Along the way I found and fixed a **real, previously-undocumented bug**: ordinary diamond inheritance (`C extends A, B` where both extend `Base`) was falsely reported as a circular reference, because sibling `extends` branches shared one cycle-detection set. Fixed by cloning it per-branch (mirroring a pattern `alias.rs` already used elsewhere) — confirmed fail→pass, documented in `docs/edge-cases.md`.

**TYPES** (4 items): AC-013 now asserts full `Diagnostic` equality; AC-004D2 covers all 11 string tags instead of 5; added a nested-NaN round-trip test covering all 6 enumerated positions. AC-005 was a genuine **spec-wording defect** (its own proving test necessarily violates its own literal wording) — amended the spec with a `#[cfg(test)]` carve-out rather than touching correct code.

**BINDING** (2 items): AC-4 extracted a pure seam so the full 65,536-call uniqueness bound is tested deterministically (the old version couldn't safely do this against the shared global counter without risking flakiness). AC-9 now uses `Arc::ptr_eq` to prove the *same* `WatchSession` is reused, not silently reconstructed.

**CLI** (3 items): Added real `extract --out` integration tests — including a symlink-based test that's the only one that actually distinguishes atomic writes from a naive `fs::write` (my first attempt didn't, and I caught that by trying to break it deliberately). Added the 5 missing LSP framing tests (AC-005b/c/d/006/007) plus the full exact-16MiB dispatch test. Added the config-path injection-safety test — confirmed it genuinely fails against a naive string-concatenation implementation with a real `SyntaxError`.

**Verification**: every fix was confirmed fail-then-pass against a deliberately reverted version where practical. Full workspace: **377 tests passing, 0 failed, clippy clean, fmt clean.**

One thing worth knowing: `docs/STATUS.md`'s test count is now further out of date (was already flagged stale in the prior session's handoff) — not something I touched, since it wasn't part of the review findings, but worth a note if you want it refreshed.

Committed as `c877ebc`. Working tree is clean aside from the two pre-existing untracked directories.

## Summary

SPEC-CLI-001a's exit-code coverage went from ~6 of 21 criteria tested to ~19 of 21 — closed AC-001, AC-003, AC-004, AC-005, AC-006, AC-011, AC-013, AC-014 (was completely untested), AC-015, AC-018, AC-020, and AC-021. The only two left uncovered (AC-009's SIGINT behavior and part of AC-010's watchexec `CriticalError` path) are exactly what the spec's own non_goals already flag as needing infrastructure this codebase doesn't have (a PTY harness) — not gaps worth chasing further.

Workspace is now at **393 Rust tests, all green, clippy clean, fmt clean**, across two commits (`b5d1108`, `c877ebc`).

What's left, in priority order: AC-001's gitignore/`.ignore`/node_modules matrix in PIPELINE — still the single most complex uncovered criterion in the whole spec set, deliberately deferred both times now. Want me to take a shot at it next, or call it here?
